title_en: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember
title_zh: Meta AI 推出最小高效模型 Muse Ember
summary_en: Meta AI released Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model for complex reasoning execution and repetitive agent tasks like tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing. It is priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for shorter prompts, matching GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, but with different long-prompt thresholds: Ember's price increases after 200k tokens, while Luna's after 272k and Haiku's after 100k. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index vs. Cost per Task chart, Muse Ember sits on the Pareto frontier, meaning no model scores higher for less cost per task. It offers six reasoning levels (minimal to max), and its output quality is comparable to Muse Wonder, which costs 40 times more.
summary_zh: Meta AI 发布了其最小、最高效的模型 Muse Ember，专为复杂推理执行和代理重复性任务（如工具调用、编码子任务、路由、提取和长文档解析）设计。对于较短提示，其定价为每百万输入 token 0.10 美元、每百万输出 token 0.50 美元，与 GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Haiku 5.5 相同，但长提示阈值不同：Ember 在 20 万 token 后涨价，Luna 在 27.2 万后，Haiku 在 10 万后。在 Artificial Analysis 的智能指数与每任务成本图表上，Muse Ember 位于帕累托前沿，意味着没有模型能以更低成本获得更高分数。它提供六个推理级别（从 minimal 到 max），输出质量与价格为其 40 倍的 Muse Wonder 相当。
content_en:
10th November 2026 - Link Blog

**Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember**. Meta AI just launched their entry in the Claude Haiku/GPT Luna category: Muse Ember, which they describe as:

\[...\] our smallest and most efficient model designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.


For shorter prompts it's priced the same as GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 - both are $0.10/million input tokens and $0.50/million output. Today's other big model release, Claude Fable 5.2, is *80x that price* at $8/$40.

The pricing is a little less straightforward as prompts get longer, though. Luna, Ember, and Haiku all support up to a million input tokens, but they also all have a threshold after which the price goes up. Taking *that* threshold into account Ember is priced between the two others:

| Model | Prompt size | Input ($/M) | Cached input | Output | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-6 Luna | ≤272k | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 | 
|  | >272k | $0.20 | $0.02 | $0.75 | 
| Muse Ember 1.0 | ≤200k | $0.10 | $0.004 | $0.50 | 
|  | >200k | $0.30 | $0.012 | $1.50 | 
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | ≤100k | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 | 
|  | >100k | $0.50 | $0.05 | $2.50 | 

But comparing price-per-token doesn't really make sense these days, when reasoning tokens mean that different models might use dramatically different numbers of tokens to solve the same problem.

For that, one measure that's useful is the Artificial Analysis.

And even more useful than that is their Intelligence Index vs. Cost per Task chart, which shows the following for those three models:

The Muse Ember models sit right on that Pareto line - the line at which you can only improve one dimension by giving up another. Meta call this out in their announcement:

It also sits on the efficiency frontier of the full Artificial Analysis leaderboard: no model scores higher for less per task.


(That grey dot on the Pareto line in the middle of the green area is GPT-6.1 Terra (low) - clearly I should be paying more attention to the Terra family!)

Muse Ember has six reasoning levels - minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, and max - so I rendered six pelicans riding bicycles. The "high" reasoning level failed to return a full SVG, and the other SVGs were surprising in that the reasoning level didn't cleanly map to the visual quality of the response.

Here's the "max" one, but the others are worth a look too:

The Ember pelicans are comparable in quality to those I got from Muse Wonder, which is 40x the price of Muse Ember.

content_zh:
2026年11月10日 - 链接博客

**推出我们最小、最高效的模型：Muse Ember**。Meta AI 刚刚在 Claude Haiku/GPT Luna 这一类别中推出了他们的产品：Muse Ember，他们将其描述为：

\[...\] 我们最小、最高效的模型，专为复杂推理执行以及智能体全天重复的工作而设计：工具调用、编码子任务、路由、提取和长文档解析。


对于较短的提示，其定价与 GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Haiku 5.5 相同——两者均为每百万输入 token 0.10 美元、每百万输出 token 0.50 美元。今天另一个重大模型发布 Claude Fable 5.2 的价格是*其 80 倍*，为 8/40 美元。

不过，随着提示变长，定价就不那么直接了。Luna、Ember 和 Haiku 都支持最多一百万输入 token，但它们也都有一个阈值，超过该阈值后价格会上涨。考虑到*这个*阈值，Ember 的定价介于另外两者之间：

| 模型 | 提示大小 | 输入（美元/百万） | 缓存输入 | 输出 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GPT-6 Luna | ≤272k | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 |
|  | >272k | $0.20 | $0.02 | $0.75 |
| Muse Ember 1.0 | ≤200k | $0.10 | $0.004 | $0.50 |
|  | >200k | $0.30 | $0.012 | $1.50 |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | ≤100k | $0.10 | $0.01 | $0.50 |
|  | >100k | $0.50 | $0.05 | $2.50 |

但如今比较每 token 价格并不真正有意义，因为推理 token 意味着不同模型在解决同一问题时可能使用截然不同数量的 token。

为此，一个有用的衡量指标是 Artificial Analysis。

比那更有用的是他们的智能指数与每任务成本图表，该图表显示了这三个模型的以下情况：

Muse Ember 模型正好位于那条帕累托线上——在这条线上，你只能通过牺牲一个维度来改善另一个维度。Meta 在他们的公告中指出了这一点：

它也位于完整 Artificial Analysis 排行榜的效率前沿上：没有模型能以更低的每任务成本获得更高的分数。


（绿色区域中间帕累托线上的那个灰点是 GPT-6.1 Terra（低）——显然我应该更关注 Terra 系列！）

Muse Ember 有六个推理级别——minimal、low、medium、high、xhigh 和 max——所以我渲染了六只骑自行车的鹈鹕。“high”推理级别未能返回完整的 SVG，而其他 SVG 令人惊讶之处在于，推理级别并没有清晰地映射到响应的视觉质量。

这是“max”的那张，但其他的也值得一看：

Ember 的鹈鹕在质量上与我从 Muse Wonder 得到的那些相当，而 Muse Wonder 的价格是 Muse Ember 的 40 倍。
